newsitem.title: USA: Malcolm X widow Betty Shabazz clinging to life.
newsitem.headline: Malcolm X widow Betty Shabazz clinging to life.

text.p: Betty Shabazz, widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, clung to life on Monday with burns over 80 percent of her body and authorities said her troubled 12-year-old grandson will be charged with setting the fire.

"She is still extremely critical. We're just happy she made it through the night," Nina Johnson, a spokeswoman at the Jacobi Hospital Burn Unit where Shabazz, 63, was being treated for third degree burns, said.
At the request of the family, the hospital would not provide any other details about her condition.

The grandson, Malcolm Shabazz, named after his controversial grandfather, Malcolm X, will be arraigned on Tuesday before a Westchester County Family Court judge on juvenile delinquency charges. Because of his age, the hearing will be closed to the public.

"The boy is a child of trauma. He is a disturbed child. In his life there has been nothing but tragedy. He has spent time in youth houses," Bill Tatum, publisher of the Amsterdam News and a close friend of Shabazz, told Reuters.

The child's mother is Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz, who was indicted in January 1995 on charges that she plotted to kill Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, whom Betty Shabazz had accused of playing a role in Malcolm X's 1965 assassination.
The indictment was dropped last month after Qubilah Shabazz completed two years of counselling.

Tatum told Reuters young Malcolm was brought to New York three weeks ago to spend time with his grandmother after his mother learned the boy was hanging out "with a rough bunch of kids" at Qubilah's San Antonio, Texas, home.

"Qubilah thought the circumstances and environment would be better for him in New York," Tatum added. But the boy rebelled and was soon hanging out "with an undesirable element in Yonkers. He kept arguing with his grandmother that he wanted to return to Texas," he said.

Shabazz was found at 1:40 a.m. EDT (0540 GMT) on Sunday in her luxury Yonkers, New York, three-bedroom co-op apartment. Tatum said the boy was alleged to have used an accelerant to start the fire by the front door of the sixth floor apartment.
"Somehow Betty was awakened and came to the door in her night clothes and tried to put the fire out," he said. "But her clothes ignited and she went up in flames herself."
Shabazz managed to get her clothes off and went to neighbours for help. "One neighbour put a sheet around her while another called police and fire departments."

Tatum said that "after allegedly setting the blaze, the boy ran out of the building and was picked up by police, wandering the streets in the nearby community of Bronxville." The Bronxville and Yonkers communities are in Westchester County, about 20 miles (32 km) north of midtown Manhattan.
Betty Shabazz heads the Office of Institutional Advancement at Medgar Evers College in Brooklyn.
